title: Lapdroid
shortDescription: Control your Android phone with your Windows keyboard and touchpad over Bluetooth.
description:
Use your laptop to control your phone. Lapdroid connects your Windows keyboard and touchpad to the Android companion app over Bluetooth. Type, tap, drag and scroll without a Wi-Fi connection.

Choose Bluetooth server or client mode, connect your paired device, then enable input capture. Press F12 to release capture and return to Windows. Use quick buttons for Android navigation, volume, playback and screenshots.

REQUIRES: Windows 10 version 1903 or later (x64), Android 8.0 or later, Bluetooth on both devices, and the free Lapdroid Android companion installed separately from https://github.com/silviuk/lapdroid/releases/latest. The Windows Store package includes only the Windows application. Android Bluetooth, overlay and Accessibility permissions are required for the companion's connection, pointer and input functions.

Bluetooth behavior and text input support can vary by device and Android app. An optional Android input method is available for apps that reject Accessibility text input. This app controls your phone; it does not mirror the phone screen on Windows.

No account is required. Input is forwarded to your connected device while capture is active. Diagnostic logs help troubleshoot connection problems; review logs before sharing them.
features: Forward keyboard input, mouse movements, taps and scrolling
Connect paired Windows and Android devices over Bluetooth
Switch between Bluetooth server and client modes
Quick Android navigation, media and volume controls
Inspect connection diagnostics in the Activity & Logs tab
certificationNotes: Windows companion for a Bluetooth Android input bridge. Requires a Bluetooth-capable Windows x64 PC and Android 8+ phone. Install the Android APK separately from https://github.com/silviuk/lapdroid/releases/tag/v0.3 (Lapdroid.apk); no login or purchase is required. Pair the devices using OS Bluetooth settings. Grant Bluetooth, overlay and Accessibility permissions in the Android app. Start Bluetooth Server on Windows, connect from the Android companion, then select Capture Input. F12 releases input. Controls & Actions and Activity & Logs can be inspected without a phone. runFullTrust is needed for native Win32 Bluetooth RFCOMM sockets, paired-device enumeration, keyboard/mouse hooks while capture is active, and optional Windows pen input injection. No elevation, services or custom drivers are required. The MSIX wraps the verified published v0.3 Lapdroid.exe without altering the executable. The Android companion is not bundled.
